issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires a modifiable List<Meal> attribute called 'orders', but the provided solution (and the surrounding template helper utilities) use arrays (Meal[]). This mismatch between 'List<Meal>' in the specification and arrays in the implementation/infrastructure (ArrayHelpers) can confuse students about which collection type to use and whether they should use ArrayHelpers or java.util.List.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and template consistent: either change the problem statement to request a modifiable Meal[] (array) for 'orders' and mention use of ArrayHelpers, or update the template/supporting code to use java.util.List<Meal> (and adjust ArrayHelpers or remove it) so students implement a List-based 'orders'. Ensure example code and UML match the chosen collection type.

issues.description: The problem text asks students to initialize the 'stock' attribute in the SealSaloon constructor, but also states that the 'stock' attribute must be static (shared across instances). Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is contradictory and may confuse students about when/how to initialize the static stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design: either (A) make 'stock' an instance final field and require students to initialize it in the constructor, or (B) keep 'stock' static/final and state that it should be initialized at declaration (or in a static initializer). Update the problem text and UML to consistently reflect the chosen approach.
